rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (score 396.3) is still the best design. Its oval finish rate is 20/20 at 1.70 s, with max_error 0.016 and zero line-loss events, so the gentle-curve controller has margin. Its failures are on s-bend (progress 0.46, max_error 0.064, 1.25 line-loss events) and slalom (progress 0.09, max_error 0.062). Those max_error values sit just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and body width is already at its maximum. Line-loss events show the tape leaves the 5-sensor array during excursions. With 12 mm footprints at x = ±0.03, a sensor only sees tape up to about 0.03 + 0.0125 + 0.006 = 0.048 m off centre, so the robot loses the line before it reaches the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.09, mass 0.5) cut oval completion to 25%, and iteration 4 (kp 5.5, kd 1.0, speed 1.05) cut it to 65%. So the gain and turn-rate changes already tried have hurt the oval, and I will not repeat them. Iteration 2 widened the array but also changed speed, footprint and wheel track together, so its s-bend result cannot be attributed to the span alone. Change: widen the outer sensors from x = ±0.03 to x = ±0.04 (spacing 2 cm), keeping the 12 mm footprint, and change nothing else from iteration 3. This extends the detectable offset to about 0.058 m, which keeps the signal alive near the off-track limit. Expected result: line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall below 1, s-bend progress rises above 0.5, and oval completion holds at 1.0. Hypotheses: (H1) the wider span is the main limit on bend survival; (H2) if oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, the larger signal swing is adding gain and kp should drop to 4.5. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, and oval completion_time.
